{{pagebanner|Welcome banner.jpg}}
'''Bashkir''' (башҡорт теле) is a Turkic language, spoken in [[Bashkortostan]], a republic in [[Russia]].

==Pronunciation guide and Alphabet==

The Bashkir alphabet is almost identical to the [[Russian_phrasebook#Pronunciation_guide|Russian alphabet]]. The differences are italicized in the list below: the Bashkir alphabet has several additional letters, and some letters that are pronounced slightly differently from their Russian counterparts. Some letters are striken through; they are included for completeness, but are not found in native Bashkir words, only Russian loanwoards.

; ''Аа'' : 	''like English f'''a'''ther {{IPA|ɑ}}''
; Бб  : like '''b'''oy {{IPA|b}}
; ''Вв''  : ''like '''w'''on {{IPA|w}}''
; ''Гг''  : ''like Russian гь, somewhat like English '''g'''eek {{IPA|ɟ}}''
; ''Ғғ''  : ''guttural R, such as in French {{IPA|ʁ}}''
; Дд  :  like '''d'''o {{IPA|d}}
; ''Ҙҙ''  : ''like '''th'''at {{IPA|ð}}''
; Ее  : like '''ye'''sterday {{IPA|je}}
; Ёё   : like '''yo'''re {{IPA|jɵ}}
; ''Жж''  : ''like English mea'''s'''ure {{IPA|ʒ}}''
; Зз    : like '''z'''oo {{IPA|z}}
; Ии    : like mach'''i'''ne {{IPA|i}}
; Йй    : like bo'''y''' {{IPA|j}}
; {{strike|Кк}}    : {{strike|like '''k'''ite {{IPA|k}}}}
; ''Ҡҡ''    : ''like Arabic '''Q'''atar; a k-sound further back in the mouth {{IPA|q}}''
; ''Лл''    : ''somewhat like English '''l'''ike {{IPA|l}}''
; Мм    : like see'''m''' {{IPA|m}}
; Нн     : like '''n'''et {{IPA|n}}
; ''Ңң''     : ''like si'''ng''' {{IPA|ŋ}}''
; Оо     : like sc'''o'''re {{IPA|o}}
; ''Өө''     : ''German ö; е pronounced with the upper lip rounded back {{IPA|ø}}''
; Пп     : like s'''p'''igot {{IPA|p}}
; Рр     : ''heavily'' rolled as in Spanish rr in pe'''rr'''o {{IPA|r}}
; Сс      : like '''s'''ailor {{IPA|s}}
; ''Ҫҫ''      : ''like '''th'''ink {{IPA|θ}}''
; Тт       : like '''t'''attoo {{IPA|t}}
; Уу       : like cart'''oo'''n {{IPA|u}}
; ''Үү''       : ''French or German y, ü; и pronounced with the upper lip rounded back {{IPA|y}}''
; {{strike|Фф}}       : {{strike|like '''f'''inish {{IPA|f}}}}
; ''Хх''  : ''a guttural sound, moreso than the Russian, as in German Ba'''ch''' {{IPA|χ}}''
; ''Һһ''  : ''like '''h'''elp {{IPA|h}}''
; {{strike|Цц}} : {{strike|like boo'''ts''' {{IPA|t͡s}}}}
; {{strike|Чч}} : {{strike|like '''ch'''eap {{IPA|t͡ɕ}}}}
; ''Шш''  : ''like English '''sh'''ot {{IPA|ʃ}}''
; ''Щщ'' : ''The same as ш''
; ''Ыы'' : ''somewhat like a curt g'''u'''t {{IPA|[ɤ̆~ʌ̆]}}''
; ''Ээ'' : ''like the letter е above''
; ''Әә''  : ''like '''a'''pple {{IPA|æ}}''
; Юю : like '''Yu'''goslavia {{IPA|ju}}
; ''Яя''       : ''like '''ya'''cht, with the а pronunciation given above {{IPA|jɑ}}'' <!-- I assume. This doesn't seem to feature in native words, so it comes down to how Bashkir speakers likely pronounce Russian а sounds. With their accents, this is the most likely realization -->

Notice that some of these differences (А, Ж, and Ш) are closer to some sounds in English than the corresponding sounds in Russian, and so should be easier to pronounce.

; PUSH : etAr (e like in pen, a like in man)

; FORBIDDEN : }}
